subject: Post-call: Vector retrofit pilot — ops & auth checklist
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@shelfwise.com>, Anika Bose <anika.bose@shelfwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Vector retrofit pilot — ops & auth checklist

Thanks again for the call today — good alignment on scope. Short recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to iterate: 

Summary of technical constraints you mentioned:
- Current vectors: 768-d from your existing provider (Pinecone).
- Peak ingest: ~120k vectors/day, average query QPS ~25, spiking to ~120 during morning batch windows.
- Storage: prefer to keep IDs and metadata in your Postgres catalog.
- Hard SLO: 80ms p90 for product search queries (web).

Redwood recommended approach (initial pilot):
1) Embedding model/dimension: start with 1536-d Redwood-embed-large for higher recall on short product descriptions — we'll provide a parallel 768-d profile for a direct compare.
2) Batching & ingest: client SDK -> batch size 64 (or adaptively 32/64 depending on token payload) using the SDKs bulk embeddings endpoint; target payload < 2MB per request to avoid gateway timeouts.
3) Normalization & similarity: store L2-normalized vectors if you intend to use cosine similarity; we recommend L2-normalize at client side to keep index consistent.
4) Index & migration: pilot with FAISS HNSW index (managed within Redwood Dedicated or your VPC depending on the environment). Migration plan: dual-write for a 1-week evaluation window, then a gradual traffic ramp (canary 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%).
5) Reranker & structured output: we suggest keeping your current TF-IDF prefix filter, run reranker as a second-stage Redwood endpoint with structured output (score + top-k ids + optional explanation tokens). This will be a separate call in the pipeline (search -> candidates -> rerank).
6) Auth & routing: for the pilot use API keys (X-Redwood-API-Key). For production we can switch to service-account JWT with KMS-managed keys. Routing policy: route read QPS to Dedicated pool in us-west with fallback to hosted small-quant model if capacity constrained.

Pilot deliverables and timeline proposal:
- Week 0: access exchange, API keys, and sample corpus (you to share ~5k representative SKUs + queries).
- Week 1: SDK onboarding + initial ingest to staging index (Aditya + Marissa to run).
- Week 2: Measurement — recall P@5, latency p50/p90, cost/unit.
- Week 3: Migration runbook & production cutover (canary).

Action items from our side:
- I will share a short ingest checklist and the embed_size_tradeoffs.pdf (attached).
- Aditya will prototype batching code for your Python ingestion pipeline.
- Marissa will prepare a simple reranker config that emits structured JSON: {"top_k": 20, "scores": true}.

Could you confirm: 1) who will own the Postgres ID mapping table during dual-write? 2) your earliest window to provide the 5k sample corpus?

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Vivek — that matches our notes. Couple clarifications from our infra side: 

- Postgres mapping: our infra team will own the canonical mapping table. We can emit a stable external_id that matches your expected id field for the pilot.
- Sample corpus: can deliver 5k SKUs + ~300 representative query logs by Thursday EOD (17 June).
- Latency SLO: 80ms p90 is aspirational; we can accept a staged SLO during pilot (200ms p90) while we tune batching and routing.

Two technical questions from Anika (cc'd):
1) For L2 normalization — does Redwood recommend normalizing client-side before indexing, or will Redwood normalize on ingest? We prefer to avoid double-transforming payloads.
2) If we migrate out of Pinecone, will you preserve our existing vector ids or do we need to re-index and create a mapping?

Appreciate the clear plan — excited to run this.

Jordan
Head of Search Engineering, Shelfwise

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Anika Bose <anika.bose@shelfwise.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@shelfwise.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:10:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Vector retrofit pilot — ops & auth checklist

Quick technical follow-up from our infra runbook perspective (copying the snippet we'll use in staging):

- Normalization: Redwood can accept either raw vectors or pre-normalized vectors. We do NOT recommend normalizing twice. Our ingest pipeline will not auto-normalize if the incoming payload contains a metadata flag: 
  - payload field: "norm_applied": true/false
If you send norm_applied=true we store as-is. If false/missing we will normalize server-side before indexing. For pilot please set norm_applied=true if you normalize client-side.

- ID preservation: We can preserve your existing external IDs. Two options: 
  1) Migrate IDs in place: export vectors from Pinecone -> ingest into Redwood with identical external_id field. This requires reindexing but preserves ids.
  2) Re-index with new internal ids + mapping table in Postgres (recommended if you want to change shard/namespace).

- Batching tips: for your average payload (short product description ~ 300 chars) we see better round-trip times at 32-64. Use the SDK's async bulk_embeddings() helper — it handles chunking and retry for transient network errors.

- Reranker contract: We'll expose a reranker endpoint that accepts {candidates: [id], query: string} and returns [{id, score, explanation}] in structured JSON. We'll also offer a streaming scoring mode if you want early cutoff for low-latency UX.

I'll attach a small example mapping file (shelfwise-mapping-example.csv) and a minimal Python snippet for bulk ingest in the Drive folder listed above.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Perfect — thanks for confirming ownership on the Postgres mapping and for the Thursday deliverable. Finalizing the kickoff plan below (I'll send calendar invites once you confirm the time):

Kickoff session (60m) — tentative: Friday 18 Jun 2027, 10:00 AM PT
Attendees: Jordan, Anika, Vivek, Marissa, Aditya, plus one infra engineer from Shelfwise
Agenda:
- Quick architecture review (10m)
- SDK onboarding demo + sample ingest (20m)
- Index config and reranker contract (15m)
- Measurement plan & rollback triggers (10m)
- Q&A / next steps (5m)

Pilot success criteria (we agreed):
- Ingest OK for 5k sample corpus with <500ms per-batch 95th percentile during staging runs.
- Retrieval P@5 improvement >= 6% vs current baseline on your labeled eval set.
- Smooth dual-write with no data loss for ID mappings.

Next steps (action owners):
- Jordan: deliver sample corpus + 300 queries (by Thu EOD).
- Anika: nominate infra engineer for kickoff (by Thu EOD).
- Aditya: drop the initial Python ingestion snippet in Drive and open an internal PR for the client helper (ETA Mon).
- Marissa: prepare staging reranker config and perf dashboard (ETA Mon).
- Vivek: send invites and share canary rollout runbook.

Attachments: embed_size_tradeoffs.pdf, shelfwise-mapping-example.csv

If that looks right I'll send the invite for Friday 10am PT.

Thanks — Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
